title: The Political Economy of Antibribery Enforcement
eligible_reason: The treatment variable l_election is a recurring Senate-election-cycle indicator for the firm's state (1 in election years, 0 otherwise); it switches on and off repeatedly in every state (verified in R1.dta: all 50 states switch from 1 to 0 at least once, e.g. state 1 is 1 in 1984, 1988, 1990, 1994, 1996, 2000, 2002). It is not an absorbing adoption at unit-specific dates. In addition every regression includes time-varying firm and state controls (size leverage cash roa salegrowth employment_rate log_population log_gdp), and the baseline columns use country, state, year and SIC fixed effects without a firm fixed effect. Tables 4 and 9 add continuous or subgroup interactions; Table 5 is a cross-section of election outcomes; Table 6 Panel B is IV.
design_notes: Firm-year panel of Compustat firms (US and foreign-headquartered) 1984-2016 (R1.dta: 137,835 obs, 8,677 gvkeys, 50 states). Outcomes: target_dummy (FCPA enforcement action), target_us_dummy, target_foreign_dummy. Key regressor l_election (election-year indicator for the senator's state). FE: country_id state_id year sic_id, plus gvkey in even columns. Cluster gvkey (state_id in some appendix columns). Table 4 interacts l_election with frac_establishments2; Table 6 regresses PAC contributions on election with state and committee FE; Table 7-8 regress segment/corruption exposure on target dummies with controls; Table 9 interacts with same_party and committee_judiciary4.

specs.exclusion_reason: non-absorbing recurring treatment; time-varying controls; no unit FE
specs.treatment_definition: Senate election year in the firm's state (switches on/off every cycle)
specs.controls: size leverage cash roa salegrowth employment_rate log_population log_gdp
specs.notes: Column 2 (line 12) adds gvkey FE; column 3 (line 14) interacts with foreign for year > 2005. Columns 4-9 repeat for target_us_dummy and target_foreign_dummy.

specs.treatment_definition: PAC contributions instrumented by election year

data_files: 7 Data and Code File/R1-DOJSEC.dta, R1-ExcludeFirst.dta, R1-Matched.dta, R1-Placebo.dta, R1-TargetYear.dta, OnlineAppendix.dta (appendix)
7 Data and Code File/D1.dta-D7.dta, D*.xlsx, Twitter.csv, Poll_Twitter.xlsx (figures)
data_files_note: Regression-ready Stata files are shipped for all tables except R5.dta (Tables 7-8), which is referenced by Tables.do but not present in the extracted package. Underlying sources (Compustat, FactSet-Revere, Orbis, RavenPack, FEC) are licensed, but the analysis files are included.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, ivreg2, outreg2); Python statsmodels for Figures 5-9.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Full-text flag ft_staggered presumably refers to the staggered timing of Senate elections across states, but the estimated model is a recurring-treatment panel regression with controls, not a staggered adoption DiD.
